svg.title: How a call flows
svg.desc: One call as the code runs it. The caller reaches the access, router or SIP trunk, and Asterisk, our own exchange, which hands the audio to the service voice. Its ear turns speech into text for the conversation core. The core asks the language model, which answers with one sentence or one tool call; the core checks the call and runs the tool, get_service_status, search_menu or draft_order, against Postgres, and hands the result back to the model, one tool per hop. The model never reads the database. The read-back goes out through the mouth. Only after the caller's yes does the core run confirm, and the model tells the caller. The order shows on the tablet; the slip prints at the register once the team approves it, in primary mode under the amount limit at once. When the AI is unsure, hears a complaint or the model fails, the call goes to the team phone, after opening hours it leaves a callback on the tablet; when the service voice itself fails, the exchange rings the team phone. Built: Conversation core, guards, Open now? get_service_status, Menu search_menu, Order draft draft_order, Confirm confirm, Postgres the facts, Order slip print bridge, Tablet approval, Push outbox, n8n. Not finished: Access router, SIP, Asterisk our exchange, Ear speech to text, Mouth text to speech, LLM understands, Team phone.
svg.text: 2 The LLM understands, the code looks up: one tool per hop, at most six.
3 The read-back goes out through the mouth.
4 The caller says yes. Only now the core confirms, and the LLM says so.
5 On the tablet; the slip prints after the team approves (primary mode: at once).
Words in (yellow), reply out (violet). One tool per hop. Confirm only after a yes.
unsure, complaint or model failure: team phone,
after hours: a callback on the tablet
the service voice fails: the exchange rings the team phone
